plan: Store the constructor's data via copy.deepcopy in a private attribute; to_data() returns another deep copy so callers can never alias internal state.

Write one recursive depth-first generator over the item tree; total_word_count() and unresolved_markers() are folds over it (notes: regex-strip [[?id]] markers then count \b\w+\b runs; references: add declared word_count / extend with unresolved list; markers deduplicated in a set and sorted).

Render outline() with a recursive walker carrying a depth counter: workspace title at depth 0 unindented, each item as two-spaces-per-level + 'kind: title', recursing into section/group items in list order.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: check both ids are strings, locate the item and its parent list by identity, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal maps to the root list; otherwise must be a section/group), reject destination == item or destination inside the item's subtree, and range-check any explicit index against the destination's current length — only after all checks pass, remove by identity and append/insert. No mutation on any error path, so a failed move trivially leaves to_data() unchanged.

Ship an in-memory unittest suite in the same file (standard library only) covering counts, markers, outline text, reorder within a list, cross-container moves, and each ValueError case with a before/after to_data() equality assertion.
mechanisms: Deep-copy isolation at both the constructor and to_data() boundary
Single recursive tree traversal shared by the word-count and marker-collection folds
Regex marker stripping ([[?\w+]]) before \b\w+\b word tokenization
Depth-carrying recursive outline renderer (two spaces per nesting level)
Validate-then-mutate move with identity-based subtree containment check, giving atomic failure for free
